classification.difficultyReason: Use perpendicular, bisecting rhombus diagonals and Pythagoras’ theorem to find half the unknown diagonal, then double it.

inlines.text: The side of a rhombus is 5 cm.
The length of one diagonal of the rhombus is 8 cm.
Find the length of the other diagonal.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of a rhombus bisect each other at right angles. Each resulting right-angled triangle has hypotenuse $5\text{ cm}$ and one shorter side of length $4\text{ cm}$. Let $l$ be half the unknown diagonal and $d$ its full length.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{8}{2}&=4\text{ cm}\\l&=\sqrt{5^2-4^2}\\l&=3\text{ cm}\\d&=2\times3\\d&=6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
